distractors.reason: We don't say 'highly friendly'. 'Highly' is used with adjectives like skilled or recommended: highly skilled, highly recommended.
We don't say 'deeply friendly'. 'Deeply' is used with feelings: deeply loyal, deeply sad.
We don't say 'strongly friendly'. 'Strongly' is used with opinions and beliefs: strongly agree, strongly believe.

l1_interference: Türkçe'de 'çok' her durumda kullanılır; İngilizcede ise 'highly' ve 'deeply' gibi kelimeler sadece belirli sıfatlarla birlikte kullanılır. 'Friendly' ile doğal olan tek seçenek 'very'dir.
explanation: In English, degree adverbs are not interchangeable. 'Very' is the general intensifier that works with most adjectives, including friendly. 'Highly' and 'deeply' combine with specific adjectives only.

related_collocations.example: My dog is deeply loyal to his owner.
This vet clinic is highly recommended.
A cat and a dog are totally different pets.

memory_tip: VERY = general intensifier (very big, very friendly) | HIGHLY = skilled, recommended | DEEPLY = feelings (deeply loyal, deeply sad)
